name: Chow Trough
line_of_business: High-volume automated food service for Tier 2 skilled workers and lower-middle-class residents
description:
Chow Trough is what Libation Corporation calls its Tier 2 brand in internal documentation. The public-facing name is different — the chain formally operates as 'C-Trough Nutrition Outlets' across most GLMZ signage — but nobody uses the formal name. Chow Trough is universal. The name is not officially embarrassing because Libation Corp long ago concluded that Tier 2 customers who know they're eating at Chow Trough will continue eating at Chow Trough because their alternative is Eat it!, and the distance between those two experiences is large enough to make the branding irrelevant.

Chow Trough locations are fully automated. There are no servers. There is a Citizen ID scanner, an order terminal with approximately 12 selections, a payment interface accepting Citizen Credit or physical chip, a preparation window, and a pickup counter. A kitchen staff of three operates behind the counter in most locations, processing orders from the automated queue. These positions are Tier 1 employment, managed through a subsidiary of a subsidiary called CTNSO Operations LLC, which exists primarily to distance Libation Corporation from the liability attached to the working conditions.

The food is caloric and nutritionally complete according to GLMZ minimum standards, which were set in 2198 and have not been updated. Protein content meets the floor. Sodium is above recommended ranges. Flavor is achieved through additive packets described on the menu as 'seasoning blends,' which are accurate. The portions are large because Tier 2 customers doing physical work require significant caloric intake and Chow Trough has learned that portion size is a powerful loyalty driver even when the portion content is undistinguished.

Chow Trough has 4,100 locations across the GLMZ, more than any other single Libation Corp brand. It is the corporation's highest-volume subsidiary by units served. It is not the most profitable.
known_products: C-Trough Standard (the baseline protein/grain plate, three size options)
C-Trough Working Meal (high-calorie variant, marketed to skilled labor)
C-Trough Card (payment chip, no loyalty integration — considered cost-ineffective at this tier)
The Big Block (oversized calorie-dense meal, unofficial menu item known by name)
